text:
incidentbot: AUTOPAGER: PagerDuty alert delivered to #eng-oncall

pagerduty: PagerDuty triggered INC-2026-0843 — kubelet NotReady on node gpu-node-142 (rack-r6). Alert: kubelet reported NotReady; node missing heartbeats. Link: <https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC-2026-0843>

Asha SRE: acked, taking. pinging serial console and checking kubelet logs. @Ben Ops FYI

Ben Ops: serial attached, host BMC reachable but kernel log shows repeated oops. snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference
[ 1234.670123] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```

Mike Eng: if kernel panic confirmed we should cordon+drain and fail pods to other pool. Recommended commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-142
kubectl drain gpu-node-142 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
```

Asha SRE: running drain now. drain output: 5/6 evicted, 1 pod stuck (statefulset, local-storage). It's a tenant-facing batch job (tenant: DataSynth). Not seeing increased 5xx at edge yet.

Sara Oncall: pinging support to run customer impact check for DataSynth — tagging as potential degraded throughput. @support-team

Ben Ops: serial shows nvme errors before panic; likely host hardware fault. Recommend RMA. Holding node out of rotation. I'll start hardware escalation and open a maintenance RMA ticket.

Asha SRE: node cordoned + marked unschedulable, pods on this node failed over except the stateful one we garbage-collected. Started canary route for DataSynth to reduce impact :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident status update — acknowledged by Asha SRE. Escalated to Hardware L2. Notifying on-call hardware channel.

Asha SRE: will hand off to Ben Ops after hardware ticket created. ETA for handoff ~20m. Leaving runbook notes in incident doc: <https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0843>

Ben Ops: hardware ticket created TKT-57821, requested RMA for NVMe and power supply. Scheduling host reboot once RMA confirmed. Marking node quarantined.

Mike Eng: creating fallback capacity for affected routing group to absorb load. Incremental autoscale in progress.

Sara Oncall: customer update sent to DataSynth via support slack thread. No major customer-facing errors detected in metrics; brief throughput dip ~4% for ~12m.

Asha SRE: handoff to Ben Ops now. If anything changes, ping @oncall. I'll follow up on pod-stateful cleanup in the morning. closing on-call message here, incident remains open with hardware team.

Ben Ops: taking over. added notes: follow-up action: root cause: NVMe driver crash -> kernel panic; RMA required. Postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
